comments.body:
If think we should avoid comparing version strings directly because the lexicographical order does not always match the version order (when their are double digits components).

```python
from sklearn.utils.fixes import sp_version, parse_version

sp_version >= parse_version("1.6.0")
```
left over debug print?

This import should probably be protected under because we will probably get an ImportError in the future (not 1.6 but in 1.8 or similar).

```python
try:
    from scipy.spatial.distance import wminkowski
except Import Error:
    # In scipy 1.6.0, wminkowski is deprecated and minkowski
    # should be used instead.
    from scipy.spatial.distance import minkowski as wminkowski
```

> Should I raise a sklearn DeprecationWarning for 'wminkowski' metric (called in sklearn/metrics/pairwise.py) or we can rely on the scipy one? Thanks!

I think we can rely on scipy one for simplicity. Maybe we could upgrade the test to also check `minkowski` with the `w` parameter in versions before 1.6.

I am running scipy 1.5 and this `w` parameter is already present.

The second part of my comment was not addressed:

> Maybe we could upgrade the test to also check minkowski with the w parameter in versions before 1.6. I am running scipy 1.5 and this w parameter is already present.

Can you give it a try?

The oldest version of scipy we support (0.19.1 as defined in `sklearn._min_dependencies`) does not have the `w` parameter for the `minkowski` function but scipy 1.0 and later do. So we could just skip this particular test parametrization for `sp_version < parse_version("1.0")` using an explicit call to `pytest.skip` such as: `pytest.skip("minkowski does not accept the w parameter prior to scipy 1.0")`.
I'm sorry @ogrisel, I was having a blind spot on the `w`. I see now that the arguments are not defined for minkowsky, they are only for wminkowsky. I will add the test ASAP.
LGTM!

We can ignore the coverage failure because all the cases cannot be tested prior to the scipy 1.6 release but the code looks correct. And even if it is not, the nightly builds will catch it quickly after the merge of this PR.

As for coverage, the `ImportError` will not trigger until scipy 1.8 is released and `wminkowski` is removed.

(This is a comment: no changes required here)
In this case, we can skip because `minkowski` is tested explicitly and this would be testing it again.

We can include the skip here:

```suggestion
         pytest.param(pairwise_distances, minkowski, _minkowski_kwds,
         			  marks=pytest.mark.skipif(sp_version < parse_version("1.0")),
         			  reason="minkoski does not accept ..."),
```
Thank you for the PR @cmarmo !
I guess this kind of parametrization should be applied to the 'minkowsi' case too, right?
I'm not sure to understand correctly: I have then skipped the wminkowski and 'wminkowski' test for scipy >=1.6.0, Is that what you meant? Thanks!

> I have then skipped the wminkowski and 'wminkowski' test for scipy >=1.6.0, Is that what you meant?

Yes this is what I meant.

I think we can skip here because this PR adds `metric = 'minkowski'` to `pytest.mark.parameterize`, so `metric = 'minkowski'` will get tested when it gets to that test case.
LGTM

#### Reference Issues/PRs
Working on the MiniBatch implementation of the Non-negative Matrix Factorization class (#16948), it has been suggested that a reformat of both standard NMF and the in progress MiniBatch implementation would improve the maintainability of the code. This pull request applies this reformatting using #14985 and #18975 as models.

#### What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.
Make `non_negative_factorization` call `NMF` instead of the opposite.

#### Any other comments?
I had to add a tag to the `NMF` class to avoid the `n_features_in` common test: but I'm not sure this was the right way to make the test pass. 
ping @TomDLT and @jeremiedbb : thanks!

comments.body: This was the correct way to validate X
I would move all these param validation in a dedicated private method, ``_check_params``, to make the code more readable and more reusable by MiniBatchNMF

I would move this in a dedicated private method, ``_initialize_W_H`` for the same reasons.
Or maybe split it into ``_initialize_W`` and ``_initialize_H`` such that we can call both in fit and only the first one in transform.
This is unecessary, let's just use the attributes everywhere

no need to move this
Edit: you already fixed it

update_H is an argument of ``non_negative_factorization`` to distinguish between fit and transform: at transform you don't update H. We don't need it in the class. In the fit we do update H and in the tranform we don't.

Actually you need to update the code of ``transform`` because it still calls the function.

Also I think that we should deprecate ``update_H`` in the function since it was there for private purpose only. wdyt @TomDLT ?
restoring the right validation should fix this.
I made a first quick pass
Yes, sorry I wasn't meant to delete those lines.
`n_components` is managed differently though: the  `test_estimators[NMF()-check_estimators_overwrite_params]` fails otherwise.
Yes, the ones that we want to modify require to pass through an auxilliary variable.

I agree we should not have `update_H` in the class.

To implement `update_H=False` in the function, we would need to either:
- create an NMF instance, fill the attributes normally added during the fit, and call transform
- or directly call the private solver functions

It makes the design a bit wonky, so I agree we could deprecate this parameter in the function.

If the purpose of having the function version is to give users control of such thing, then removing it for the sake of a code cleanup might be throwing out the baby with the bath water. Is it not more appropriate to create a private class underlying NMF but also facilitating this need through the availability of extra parameters or controls?

Fair point, it would remove a functionality, which is using the NMF `transform` without the `fit` first. I am not sure this is not something we generally want to support in scikit-learn estimators, so if we want to keep this use-case, I think we should keep the current organization and not do the proposed refactoring.
Perhaps the question is then not just whether update_H should be in the class, but whether it's useful to a subset of users, or whether it was only there for the convenience of the developer.

My intuition is that this use case is not a non-negative matrix factorization use case but an ElasticNet problem with positivity constraint on the coefs which can actually be done (``ElasticNet(positive=True)``).

EDIT: only true with the beta_divergence=2, so there might still be a need, although I still think it's not a matrix factorization problem then.
If we want to keep this possibility we could add a ``H`` parameter to the transform method such that if it's not None, we allow to transform without having calling fit.

Hello everyone I need some help about `n_features_in_`
I have a number of tests failing with the error
```
E           AttributeError: 'NMF' object has no attribute 'n_components_'
```
from the lines
https://github.com/cmarmo/scikit-learn/blob/d4eeb7861947cb352080f13993dcbfb5a5ca1ef7/sklearn/decomposition/_nmf.py#L1394-L1396

I put here a snippet having the same problem
```py
import numpy as np
from sklearn.decomposition import non_negative_factorization

rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
X = rng.random_sample((20, 15))
H = rng.random_sample((15, 15))
W = rng.random_sample((20, 15))

non_negative_factorization(X, H=H, update_H=False)
```
Apparently the `check_is_fitted(self)` function thinks the estimator is fitted because `attrs` contains `'n_features_in_'`, see
https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/blob/4beb0c27fc0439c12dad244fe4063e96f8983a52/sklearn/utils/validation.py#L1040
(I have temporarily added a `print(attrs)` to check). Is that an expected behavior? Thanks!

> Hello everyone I need some help about n_features_in_

Let's forget the idea of being able to call transform without fit. It makes the code too complicated. That way this PR is completely transparent to the user and doesn't change the API at all. I directly pushed this.
The latest changes in the PR keep the behavior of update_H. The public API and functionalities aren't modified at all. I'll resolve the conversation now.
This function should be a method of the class. Same remark for _check_w_h
Knowing that MiniBatchNMF will follow why not leaving _check_w_h and _check_params outside the class as they could be reused? This is the same for eg _check_init, am I wrong?
MiniBatchNMF will inherit from NMF so it will have access to these methods
I think that _check_init and some others should also be methods of the class but I didn't say it to not make the diff too big

I find very confusing as a non-expert reader the idea of putting some functions in the class and some other not: I can't see the reason to make a difference. I'm happy to learn if there is one, but could we put all the functions in the same place if not? Thanks.

To me the functions meant to validate class parameters should definitely be methods. They're not and never will be used outside of the class. For the functions that "do the math" I don't think it's mandatory. We can imagine them being used somewhere else, and leaving them as functions makes them a bit easier to unit test.

I'd rather have the new functions be put in the right place right away. The other ones can be moved in this PR or later. For my part I find it more confusing to introduce new code in a place that I think it should not be.
Now that it's a method we can use the attributes instead of passing them as arguments.
I would put that in _check_params and define a new attribute self._n_components to store it
thanks @cmarmo. I just have one last remark
Should I pass X to the method then? Or n_features?
I'd say X but no strong opinion

Just to clarify, this change was not really needed because it was already the default value for the `update_H` param in master and the goal is just to make the test more explicit, right?

I assume this PR should not change the behavior of the public methods and therefore this test would not need this to pass.
